items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the general business law, in relation to enacting "the toll
payer protection act"

A.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to enacting the "toll
payer protection act"; and to repeal certain provisions of such law relating
thereto
A.lawCode: Rpld §2985, add Art 9 Title 11-A §§2985 & 2985-a, Pub Auth L

summary: Enacts the "toll payer protection act" to establish a New York toll payers' bill of rights; provides that any person, firm, corporation, or other entity who is charged with the payment of a cashless toll fee in the state of New York shall have the option to be notified by text message or electronic mail that such fee has been so charged, the entity to which such fee must be paid, and the date by when such fee must be paid; further provides for the establishment of a payment plan for the payment of a toll fee and any related penalties; makes related provisions.
title: Enacts the "toll payer protection act"; repealer

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 341
 
TO THE ASSEMBLY:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Assembly Bill Number 9805-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to enacting
      the  "toll payer protection act"; and to repeal certain provisions
      of such law relating thereto"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This legislation makes a number of substantial and systemically  prob-
lematic  changes  to  the capability of toll authorities to both collect
tolls and enforce toll violations within the state of New  York  to  the
detriment  of  the end users of the system, and the efficient and neces-
sary operation of these authorities.
 
  Open road, cashless tolling is  critical  to  modernizing  New  York's
roadways,  easing  congestion, and reimagining our transportation system
for the 21st century economy. Transitioning the State to cashless  toll-
ing  not  only improves the safety of motorists, it reduces carbon emis-
sions and helps further the State's efforts to  provide  a  greener  and
more modern New York for all.
 
  The Thruway Authority, MTA Bridges and Tunnels, and the Port Authority
of  New  York  and New Jersey have taken significant actions to ensure a
fair and balanced  approach  to  toll  billing  and  collection.  Recent
actions include: establishing a "tolls by mail" website for online look-
up and payment of toll bills; creating a more informative billing envel-
ope,  establishing  additional  mailing,  and adding messaging to bills;
engaging in efforts to ensure drivers update their registration informa-
tion for billing purposes; implementing of  a  "First  Call  Resolution"
pilot  program;  posting additional fee signage on the systems; resizing
and expanding telecom infrastructure to support increased volume  calls;
implementing  pilot programs to eliminate fees on first violation notice
to E-Z Pass  customers;  ensuring  vendor  accountability  for  contract
compliance; and reducing fees and amnesty programs.
 
  The legislation in question, however, lowers to the point of insignif-
icance,  any penalty that could be charged for nonpayment of a toll bill
and prohibits registration suspension for nonpayment,  hamstringing  the
State's  enforcement  ability.  Fairness for all users demands that toll
evaders who flout the law pay their fair  share.    Instead,  this  bill
would  facilitate greater toll evasion, putting a greater financial onus
on law abiding users, which is untenable. We should be facilitating toll
payer equity, not abolishing it.
 
  Open road, cashless tolling is becoming  the  norm  in  the  northeast
region,  and  recently,  the  State Department of Motor Vehicles and the
aforementioned authorities have  signed  a  reciprocity  agreement  with
Massachusetts,   that  will  provide  further  regional  uniformity  and
accountability for multistate toll violators. More of  these  agreements
must  be  executed  to  ensure toll payer equity across the region. This
legislation, however, would  effectively  undercut  this  agreement  and
prevent any future agreements from going into effect.
 
  More can always be done, and, to ensure a fair and efficient system, I
will propose additional enhancements to benefit all system users in next
year's  Executive  budget.  For  the aforementioned reasons I am vetoing
this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                               __________
